The retrieved documents consistently state that peaches originated in China [d1, d2, d3, d5, d6, d7, d8, d9]. Differences are only in the level of detail (e.g., specific domestication dates or regions within China) or in discussing later spread and modern production, which do not contradict the core origin claim.

All relevant evidence points to the same answer: peaches come from China. The documents provide complementary details about domestication history and subsequent global spread, but there is no disagreement on the place of origin.

Peaches originated in China [d1, d2, d3, d5, d6, d7, d8, d9]. They were first domesticated there, with archaeological evidence pointing to the Yangtze River Valley as early as 6000 BCE [d1, d2]. From China, peaches spread westward through Asia to the Mediterranean and later to Europe and the Americas via Spanish explorers [d8, d9].
